hook.h2: He says you will find Him if you look
hook.text: Then you will call on me, come, and pray to me, and I will listen to you. You will seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.
father: Then you will call on me, come, and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
You will seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.
hook.note: This is not a verse about people who already believe. It is addressed to people a long way from home, and it makes a plain, testable promise: look honestly, and you will find. Every word of it is our Father speaking, which is why the whole passage is BLUE — and that is the whole point of this Bible. You are not being asked to take someone's word for what He is like. You can see which words are His and read them yourself.

short350: You may have come to this book from another faith, or from none. You are welcome to read it as it is. Nobody has to agree to anything first.
Father's Heart Bible is the first Bible in print where you can see who is speaking.
Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's in RED. The Spirit's in PURPLE.

For a hundred and twenty-five years, red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking. The color marks ownership, not quotation: His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, words He never spoke are never colored, and narration stays black.

That matters more here than anywhere else. If you are reading the Bible to find out what God is actually like rather than what people say about Him, the first thing you need is to know which lines are His. In this edition you can see them at a glance, on every page, from Genesis to Revelation.

In Athens, Paul did not attack what people believed. He pointed at their own altar to a god they had not named, quoted their own poets back to them, and told them who they had been reaching for all along: "so they might seek our Father, perhaps reach for him and find him — though he is not far from each of us."
That is what this Bible was made to do. Not to tell you about a Father who speaks, but to show you where He already has.

He is not distant. He is not disappointed. He is your Heavenly Father, and He delights in you as His beloved child. If father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you: the Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood, but the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.

An introduction opens each book so you know what you are walking into, a Father's note closes each with a short prayer, and 1,354 notes serve the reader, not the scholar — explaining a word, a name, a custom or a piece of background as it comes up, rather than assuming you already know it. A presentation page carries a name. Six by nine, hardcover, full color throughout.
A fresh translation from the original Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek — complete, 66 books and 31,085 verses. A gift, a keepsake, an heirloom.
Receive the Father. Hear His voice. His heart is for you.

long.h: Receive The Father. Hear His Voice. His Heart Is For You.
body: The Seeker's Bible is a color coded Bible for seekers, skeptics, and anyone exploring the Christian faith for the first time — the first Bible in print where you can see who is speaking.
Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's words in RED. The Spirit's words in PURPLE.

For a hundred and twenty-five years, the red letter Bible has shown you the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. He has been speaking the whole time. No Bible has ever shown you where.

That is the practical reason this edition exists for a first reader. Open any page and you can tell the difference between what a divine person said and what somebody wrote down about Him — without a teacher, a class, or a background in any of it.

long.h: You May Have Come To This Book From Another Faith, Or From None
body: You are welcome to read it as it is. Everyone needs the Father. There is no membership, no vocabulary test, and no point at which you are expected to stop asking questions.

When Paul stood in Athens he did not attack what the people there already believed. He told them he could see how religious they were, pointed at their own altar to a god they had not named, and quoted their own poets back to them. Then he told them who they had been reaching for all along. "What you worship without knowing it, I now proclaim to you." — Acts 17:23
He is not far from you either. Read it for yourself, and see who is speaking.

If you have never done this before, start with the book of John. It is the fourth book of the New Testament, it begins about two-thirds of the way through this volume, and it is where the claim at the center of the whole thing is made most plainly. There is an introduction at the head of it telling you what it is and who wrote it.

long.h: A Three Color Bible: Red Letter, Blue Letter, Purple Letter
body: The color is a mark of ownership, not of quotation. His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, and words He never spoke are never colored. Our Father speaks 125,457 words here. The Son speaks 39,936. More than one word in four of this Bible is a divine person speaking.

Narration stays black. So does every human speech — the arguments, the complaints, the bad advice, the things people say about God that turn out to be wrong. A skeptic's fairest objection to religious writing is that it blurs the two, and this edition draws the line on the page instead of leaving it to be taken on trust.

God is our Father. Not a role He plays. Father is who He is, and Father is His name, the name Jesus came to reveal: "I revealed your name to those you gave me from the world" (John 17:6). This translation lets the Hebrew and Greek speak the distinction they always made: God as Father, Abba Father, your Heavenly Father — and you, His beloved child.

Notice who, in Scripture, speaks of Him only as a distant deity and never as Father: the serpent in Eden, Pharaoh, the accusers in Job, the tempter in the wilderness. The caricature of a remote and disappointed God is not the Bible's picture of Him. It is the picture His enemies keep painting, and the text itself keeps correcting.

If the word father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you. The Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood. He is the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.

faq.q: I'm not a Christian. Is this Bible still for me?
faq.a: Yes — it was made with you in mind. You are welcome to read it as it is, from wherever you are starting, and nothing in it asks you to agree before you begin. The opening pages say so plainly: you may have come to this book from another faith, or from none. What the Divine Voice Color gives you is the ability to tell, on any page, which words are claimed as a divine person's own and which are somebody's account of events — so you can weigh the claim yourself instead of taking a summary of it from anyone.

The book of John, about two-thirds of the way in. It is the shortest route to the central claim, and every one of the 66 books opens with an introduction telling you what it is, who wrote it and what it is doing there. If you would rather see it before you buy it, the entire translation is free to read at fathersheartbible.com/read.

faq.q: What makes the Seeker's Bible different from the other editions?
faq.a: It is the complete Father's Heart Bible™ in Divine Voice Color — every book, every page, nothing abridged — bound and opened for someone reading it for the first time. The cover and the opening pages are what change: a word to the reader who has come from another faith or from none, a prayer nobody is obliged to pray, and passages on intimacy, identity and inheritance chosen for someone still deciding. From Genesis 1:1 onward the text is identical to every other edition.

It is the complete Bible, and the 1,354 notes are there to serve you rather than a scholar — they explain a word, a name, a custom or a piece of background where it would otherwise pass you by. What you are mainly holding is our Father speaking for Himself, in BLUE, which is a thing you can weigh directly without anyone standing between you and it.

faq.q: How do I know the coloring is honest?
faq.a: Because it follows one rule you can check yourself on any page: color marks who spoke the words, not who is quoting them. Our Father's words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, words He never spoke are never colored, and narration stays black. Read a page at fathersheartbible.com/read and test it against a translation you already trust.

faq.q: Do I have to buy it to read it?
faq.a: Every word is free to read online in twenty-five languages, and English and Telugu are free to listen to as well. Our Father's voice was never behind a price — receiving Him costs nothing. The print edition is for people who want it in their hands, or want to give it.
